root_cause.text: pppol2tp_ioctl() directly accessed sock->sk->sk_user_data (the l2tp_session pointer) without any reference counting or locking, enabling a concurrent socket close to free the session while the ioctl thread could sleep via copy_from_user(), leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "pppol2tp_ioctl() read sock->sk->sk_user_data directly without any locks or reference counting. If a controllable sleep was induced during copy_from_user() ... a concurrent socket close could trigger pppol2tp_session_close() asynchronously. This frees the l2tp_session structure ... Upon resuming, the ioctl thread dereferences the stale session pointer, resulting in a Use-After-Free (UAF)." The patch replaces the direct access with the RCU-safe, refcounted helper pppol2tp_sock_to_session() and ensures l2tp_session_put() is called on all exit paths.
